page: Microsoft Azure D2_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The compute topology provides 2 dedicated vCPUs executed across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, paired with 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware features include 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, 48 MB L3 cache, and instruction set support for AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI. The server includes no bundled local storage and contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread performance alongside bounded multi-thread throughput inherent to a single-core physical topology. Stress-ng records 1889.98 in single-core execution and 1931.58 in multi-core testing. Geekbench yields 1596.0 for single-core and 1851.0 for multi-core compute. Memory throughput registers at 14.67 GB/s for uncached reads and 13.65 GB/s for writes. In application-focused metrics, the system delivers 1.95 million operations per second in Redis SET operations, 3.62 GB/s in static web serving throughput, and 77.85 tokens per second in 135M small-model text generation.

Without local ephemeral storage, disk operations rely entirely on remote storage attachments. The allocation of 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of memory makes the instance functionally tailored to modest workloads such as lightweight web servers, API endpoints, microservices, development environments, and low-intensity background utilities.
